running_head: A Grammar, Vocabularies and Exercises for Sections One–Twenty

blocks.text: ἀπολοίμην (sometimes just ὀλοίμην) means ‘May I die! Damn me!’ (cf. the stem ἀπολ- learned at vocabulary 8C). This use of the optative on its own to express a wish for the future is very common. It will be fully introduced later on.

You have already met some verbs ending in -μι, e.g. εἰ-μί, ‘I am’, εἶ-μι ‘I shall go’ and φημί ‘I say’ (see 386–8). You have noticed that they are quite different from verbs in -ω.
There are a number of such verbs in Greek, of which the most common are:

δίδωμι ‘I give’
τίθημι ‘I place’
ἵημι ‘I let go, shoot’
ἵστημι ‘I set up’
δείκνυμι ‘I show’
Here now, in full, is the conjugation of δίδωμι. It will give you the key to all -μι verbs. Know δίδωμι, and the rest will be relatively straightforward:
